paragraphs.text: And as he passed by, he saw a man blind from his birth.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ παράγων εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον τυφλὸν ἐκ γενετῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai paragōn eiden anthrōpon typhlon ek genetēs.

paragraphs.text: And his disciples asked him, saying, Rabbi, who sinned, this man, or his parents, that he should be born blind?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Ῥαββί, τίς ἥμαρτεν, οὗτος ἢ οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἵνα τυφλὸς γεννηθῇ;
paragraphs.translit: kai ērōtēsan auton hoi mathētai autou legontes· Rhabbi, tis hēmarten, houtos ē hoi goneis autou, hina typhlos gennēthē;

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered, Neither did this man sin, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Οὔτε οὗτος ἥμαρτεν οὔτε οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἀλλʼ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous· Oute houtos hēmarten oute hoi goneis autou, allʼ hina phanerōthē ta erga tou theou en autō.

paragraphs.text: We must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.
paragraphs.original: ἡμᾶς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ πέμψαντός με ἕως ἡμέρα ἐστίν· ἔρχεται νὺξ ὅτε οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐργάζεσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: hēmas dei ergazesthai ta erga tou pempsantos me heōs hēmera estin· erchetai nyx hote oudeis dynatai ergazesthai.

paragraphs.text: When I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ὦ, φῶς εἰμι τοῦ κόσμου.
paragraphs.translit: hotan en tō kosmō ō, phōs eimi tou kosmou.

paragraphs.text: When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and anointed his eyes with the clay,
paragraphs.original: ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἔπτυσεν χαμαὶ καὶ ἐποίησεν πηλὸν ἐκ τοῦ πτύσματος, καὶ ἐπέχρισεν αὐτοῦ τὸν πηλὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς,
paragraphs.translit: tauta eipōn eptysen chamai kai epoiēsen pēlon ek tou ptysmatos, kai epechrisen autou ton pēlon epi tous ophthalmous,

paragraphs.text: and said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam (which is by interpretation, Sent). He went away therefore, and washed, and came seeing.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε νίψαι εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν τοῦ Σιλωάμ (ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Ἀπεσταλμένος). ἀπῆλθεν οὖν καὶ ἐνίψατο, καὶ ἦλθεν βλέπων.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autō· Hypage nipsai eis tēn kolymbēthran tou Silōam (ho hermēneuetai Apestalmenos). apēlthen oun kai enipsato, kai ēlthen blepōn.

paragraphs.text: The neighbors therefore, and they that saw him aforetime, that he was a beggar, said, Is not this he that sat and begged?
paragraphs.original: οἱ οὖν γείτονες καὶ οἱ θεωροῦντες αὐτὸν τὸ πρότερον ὅτι προσαίτης ἦν ἔλεγον· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ καθήμενος καὶ προσαιτῶν;
paragraphs.translit: hoi oun geitones kai hoi theōrountes auton to proteron hoti prosaitēs ēn elegon· Ouch houtos estin ho kathēmenos kai prosaitōn;

paragraphs.text: Others said, It is he: others said, No, but he is like him. He said, I am [he].
paragraphs.original: ἄλλοι ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν· ἄλλοι ἔλεγον· Οὐχί, ἀλλὰ ὅμοιος αὐτῷ ἐστιν. ἐκεῖνος ἔλεγεν ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι.
paragraphs.translit: alloi elegon hoti Houtos estin· alloi elegon· Ouchi, alla homoios autō estin. ekeinos elegen hoti Egō eimi.

paragraphs.text: They said therefore unto him, How then were thine eyes opened?
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ· Πῶς ἠνεῴχθησάν σου οἱ ὀφθαλμοί;
paragraphs.translit: elegon oun autō· Pōs ēneōchthēsan sou hoi ophthalmoi;

paragraphs.text: He answered, The man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and said unto me, Go to Siloam, and wash: so I went away and washed, and I received sight.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος· Ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰησοῦς πηλὸν ἐποίησεν καὶ ἐπέχρισέν μου τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ εἶπέν μοι ὅτι Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν Σιλωὰμ καὶ νίψαι· ἀπελθὼν οὖν καὶ νιψάμενος ἀνέβλεψα.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē ekeinos· Ho anthrōpos ho legomenos Iēsous pēlon epoiēsen kai epechrisen mou tous ophthalmous kai eipen moi hoti Hypage eis ton Silōam kai nipsai· apelthōn oun kai nipsamenos aneblepsa.

paragraphs.text: And they said unto him, Where is he? He saith, I know not.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος; λέγει· Οὐκ οἶδα.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipan autō· Pou estin ekeinos; legei· Ouk oida.

paragraphs.text: They bring to the Pharisees him that aforetime was blind.
paragraphs.original: Ἄγουσιν αὐτὸν πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους τόν ποτε τυφλόν.
paragraphs.translit: Agousin auton pros tous Pharisaious ton pote typhlon.

paragraphs.text: Now it was the sabbath on the day when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ τὸν πηλὸν ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἀνέῳξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de sabbaton en hē hēmera ton pēlon epoiēsen ho Iēsous kai aneōxen autou tous ophthalmous.

paragraphs.text: Again therefore the Pharisees also asked him how he received his sight. And he said unto them, He put clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and I see.
paragraphs.original: πάλιν οὖν ἠρώτων αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πῶς ἀνέβλεψεν. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πηλὸν ἐπέθηκέν μου ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς, καὶ ἐνιψάμην, καὶ βλέπω.
paragraphs.translit: palin oun ērōtōn auton kai hoi Pharisaioi pōs aneblepsen. ho de eipen autois· Pēlon epethēken mou epi tous ophthalmous, kai enipsamēn, kai blepō.

paragraphs.text: Some therefore of the Pharisees said, This man is not from God, because he keepeth not the sabbath. But others said, How can a man that is a sinner do such signs? And there was division among them.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγον οὖν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων τινές· Οὐκ ἔστιν οὗτος παρὰ θεοῦ ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὅτι τὸ σάββατον οὐ τηρεῖ. ἄλλοι ἔλεγον· Πῶς δύναται ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλὸς τοιαῦτα σημεῖα ποιεῖν; καὶ σχίσμα ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: elegon oun ek tōn Pharisaiōn tines· Ouk estin houtos para theou ho anthrōpos, hoti to sabbaton ou tērei. alloi elegon· Pōs dynatai anthrōpos hamartōlos toiauta sēmeia poiein; kai schisma ēn en autois.

paragraphs.text: They say therefore unto the blind man again, What sayest thou of him, in that he opened thine eyes? And he said, He is a prophet.
paragraphs.original: λέγουσιν οὖν τῷ τυφλῷ πάλιν· Τί σὺ λέγεις περὶ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν ὅτι Προφήτης ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: legousin oun tō typhlō palin· Ti sy legeis peri autou, hoti ēneōxen sou tous ophthalmous; ho de eipen hoti Prophētēs estin.

paragraphs.text: The Jews therefore did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind, and had received his sight, until they called the parents of him that had received his sight,
paragraphs.original: Οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἦν τυφλὸς καὶ ἀνέβλεψεν, ἕως ὅτου ἐφώνησαν τοὺς γονεῖς αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἀναβλέψαντος
paragraphs.translit: Ouk episteusan oun hoi Ioudaioi peri autou hoti ēn typhlos kai aneblepsen, heōs hotou ephōnēsan tous goneis autou tou anablepsantos

paragraphs.text: and asked them, saying, Is this your son, who ye say was born blind? How then doth he now see?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτοὺς λέγοντες· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ὑμῶν, ὃν ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη; πῶς οὖν βλέπει ἄρτι;
paragraphs.translit: kai ērōtēsan autous legontes· Houtos estin ho hyios hymōn, hon hymeis legete hoti typhlos egennēthē; pōs oun blepei arti;

paragraphs.text: His parents answered and said, We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind:
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπαν· Οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ἡμῶν καὶ ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη·
paragraphs.translit: apekrithēsan oun hoi goneis autou kai eipan· Oidamen hoti houtos estin ho hyios hēmōn kai hoti typhlos egennēthē·

paragraphs.text: but how he now seeth, we know not; or who opened his eyes, we know not: ask him; he is of age; he shall speak for himself.
paragraphs.original: πῶς δὲ νῦν βλέπει οὐκ οἴδαμεν, ἢ τίς ἤνοιξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἡμεῖς οὐκ οἴδαμεν· αὐτὸν ἐρωτήσατε, ἡλικίαν ἔχει, αὐτὸς περὶ ἑαυτοῦ λαλήσει.
paragraphs.translit: pōs de nyn blepei ouk oidamen, ē tis ēnoixen autou tous ophthalmous hēmeis ouk oidamen· auton erōtēsate, hēlikian echei, autos peri heautou lalēsei.

paragraphs.text: These things said his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man should confess him [to be] Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.
paragraphs.original: ταῦτα εἶπαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐφοβοῦντο τοὺς Ἰουδαίους, ἤδη γὰρ συνετέθειντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἵνα ἐάν τις αὐτὸν ὁμολογήσῃ χριστόν, ἀποσυνάγωγος γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: tauta eipan hoi goneis autou hoti ephobounto tous Ioudaious, ēdē gar synetetheinto hoi Ioudaioi hina ean tis auton homologēsē christon, aposynagōgos genētai.

paragraphs.text: Therefore said his parents, He is of age; ask him.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπαν ὅτι Ἡλικίαν ἔχει, αὐτὸν ἐπερωτήσατε.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto hoi goneis autou eipan hoti Hēlikian echei, auton eperōtēsate.

paragraphs.text: So they called a second time the man that was blind, and said unto him, Give glory to God: we know that this man is a sinner.
paragraphs.original: Ἐφώνησαν οὖν τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐκ δευτέρου ὃς ἦν τυφλὸς καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δὸς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ· ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: Ephōnēsan oun ton anthrōpon ek deuterou hos ēn typhlos kai eipan autō· Dos doxan tō theō· hēmeis oidamen hoti houtos ho anthrōpos hamartōlos estin.

paragraphs.text: He therefore answered, Whether he is a sinner, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη οὖν ἐκεῖνος· Εἰ ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν οὐκ οἶδα· ἓν οἶδα ὅτι τυφλὸς ὢν ἄρτι βλέπω.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē oun ekeinos· Ei hamartōlos estin ouk oida· hen oida hoti typhlos ōn arti blepō.

paragraphs.text: They said therefore unto him, What did he to thee? How opened he thine eyes?
paragraphs.original: εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ· Τί ἐποίησέν σοι; πῶς ἤνοιξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς;
paragraphs.translit: eipon oun autō· Ti epoiēsen soi; pōs ēnoixen sou tous ophthalmous;

paragraphs.text: He answered them, I told you even now, and ye did not hear; wherefore would ye hear it again? would ye also become his disciples?
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς· Εἶπον ὑμῖν ἤδη καὶ οὐκ ἠκούσατε· τί πάλιν θέλετε ἀκούειν; μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε αὐτοῦ μαθηταὶ γενέσθαι;
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē autois· Eipon hymin ēdē kai ouk ēkousate· ti palin thelete akouein; mē kai hymeis thelete autou mathētai genesthai;

paragraphs.text: And they reviled him, and said, Thou art his disciple; but we are disciples of Moses.
paragraphs.original: ἐλοιδόρησαν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπον· Σὺ μαθητὴς εἶ ἐκείνου, ἡμεῖς δὲ τοῦ Μωϋσέως ἐσμὲν μαθηταί·
paragraphs.translit: eloidorēsan auton kai eipon· Sy mathētēs ei ekeinou, hēmeis de tou Mōyseōs esmen mathētai·

paragraphs.text: We know that God hath spoken unto Moses: but as for this man, we know not whence he is.
paragraphs.original: ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι Μωϋσεῖ λελάληκεν ὁ θεός, τοῦτον δὲ οὐκ οἴδαμεν πόθεν ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: hēmeis oidamen hoti Mōysei lelalēken ho theos, touton de ouk oidamen pothen estin.

paragraphs.text: The man answered and said unto them, Why, herein is the marvel, that ye know not whence he is, and [yet] he opened mine eyes.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐν τούτῳ γὰρ τὸ θαυμαστόν ἐστιν ὅτι ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε πόθεν ἐστίν, καὶ ἤνοιξέν μου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē ho anthrōpos kai eipen autois· En toutō gar to thaumaston estin hoti hymeis ouk oidate pothen estin, kai ēnoixen mou tous ophthalmous.

paragraphs.text: We know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and do his will, him he heareth.
paragraphs.original: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἁμαρτωλῶν ὁ θεὸς οὐκ ἀκούει, ἀλλʼ ἐάν τις θεοσεβὴς ᾖ καὶ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιῇ τούτου ἀκούει.
paragraphs.translit: oidamen hoti hamartōlōn ho theos ouk akouei, allʼ ean tis theosebēs ē kai to thelēma autou poiē toutou akouei.

paragraphs.text: Since the world began it was never heard that any one opened the eyes of a man born blind.
paragraphs.original: ἐκ τοῦ αἰῶνος οὐκ ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν τις ὀφθαλμοὺς τυφλοῦ γεγεννημένου·
paragraphs.translit: ek tou aiōnos ouk ēkousthē hoti ēneōxen tis ophthalmous typhlou gegennēmenou·

paragraphs.text: If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.
paragraphs.original: εἰ μὴ ἦν οὗτος παρὰ θεοῦ, οὐκ ἠδύνατο ποιεῖν οὐδέν.
paragraphs.translit: ei mē ēn houtos para theou, ouk ēdynato poiein ouden.

paragraphs.text: They answered and said unto him, Thou wast altogether born in sins, and dost thou teach us? And they cast him out.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἐν ἁμαρτίαις σὺ ἐγεννήθης ὅλος, καὶ σὺ διδάσκεις ἡμᾶς; καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithēsan kai eipan autō· En hamartiais sy egennēthēs holos, kai sy didaskeis hēmas; kai exebalon auton exō.

paragraphs.text: Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and finding him, he said, Dost thou believe on the Son of God?
paragraphs.original: Ἤκουσεν Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω, καὶ εὑρὼν αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Σὺ πιστεύεις εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousen Iēsous hoti exebalon auton exō, kai heurōn auton eipen· Sy pisteueis eis ton hyion tou anthrōpou;

paragraphs.text: He answered and said, And who is he, Lord, that I may believe on him?
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν· Καὶ τίς ἐστιν, κύριε, ἵνα πιστεύσω εἰς αὐτόν;
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē ekeinos kai eipen· Kai tis estin, kyrie, hina pisteusō eis auton;

paragraphs.text: Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and he it is that speaketh with thee.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Καὶ ἑώρακας αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετὰ σοῦ ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: eipen autō ho Iēsous· Kai heōrakas auton kai ho lalōn meta sou ekeinos estin.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Πιστεύω, κύριε· καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ephē· Pisteuō, kyrie· kai prosekynēsen autō.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said, For judgment came I into this world, that they that see not may see; and that they that see may become blind.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰς κρίμα ἐγὼ εἰς τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον ἦλθον, ἵνα οἱ μὴ βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ οἱ βλέποντες τυφλοὶ γένωνται.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen ho Iēsous· Eis krima egō eis ton kosmon touton ēlthon, hina hoi mē blepontes blepōsin kai hoi blepontes typhloi genōntai.

paragraphs.text: Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said unto him, Are we also blind?
paragraphs.original: ἤκουσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων ταῦτα οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὄντες, καὶ εἶπον αὐτῷ· Μὴ καὶ ἡμεῖς τυφλοί ἐσμεν;
paragraphs.translit: ēkousan ek tōn Pharisaiōn tauta hoi metʼ autou ontes, kai eipon autō· Mē kai hēmeis typhloi esmen;

paragraphs.text: Jesus said unto them, If ye were blind, ye would have no sin: but now ye say, We see: your sin remaineth.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰ τυφλοὶ ἦτε, οὐκ ἂν εἴχετε ἁμαρτίαν· νῦν δὲ λέγετε ὅτι Βλέπομεν· ἡ ἁμαρτία ὑμῶν μένει.
paragraphs.translit: eipen autois ho Iēsous· Ei typhloi ēte, ouk an eichete hamartian· nyn de legete hoti Blepomen· hē hamartia hymōn menei.
